verified_quotes.exact_text: Table 1 of this section lists the violation categories and other situations requiring a Tier 1 public notice.
Provide a public notice as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the violation or situation requiring Tier 1 public notice

Initiate consultation with the primacy agency as soon as practical, but no later than 24 hours after the public water system learns of the violation or situation, to determine additional public notice requirements
Public water systems must provide the notice within 24 hours in a form and manner reasonably calculated to reach all persons served.
Appropriate broadcast media (such as radio and television);
Posting of the notice in conspicuous locations throughout the area served by the water system;
Hand delivery of the notice to persons served by the water system; or
Another delivery method approved in writing by the primacy agency.

Violation of the MCL for total coliforms when fecal coliform or E. coli are present in the water distribution system (as specified in § 141.63(b)), or when the water system fails to test for fecal coliforms or E. coli when any repeat sample tests positive for coliform (as specified in § 141.21(e)); Violation of the MCL for E. coli (as specified in § 141.63(c));
Exceedance of the Action Level for lead as specified in § 141.80(c).

Violation of the MCL for nitrate, nitrite, or total nitrate and nitrite, as defined in § 141.62, or when the water system fails to take a confirmation sample within 24 hours of the system's receipt of the first sample showing an exceedance of the nitrate or nitrite MCL, as specified in § 141.23(f)(2);

Violation of the MRDL for chlorine dioxide, as defined in § 141.65(a), when one or more samples taken in the distribution system the day following an exceedance of the MRDL at the entrance of the distribution system exceed the MRDL, or when the water system does not take the required samples in the distribution system, as specified in § 141.133(c)(2)(i);
